stimuli.title: Gita, Charu, Lata, Nisha, Uma, Pia, Aditi, Kiran attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.
stimuli.body:

• Lata occupies March 21.
• Nisha and Pia attend in consecutive interview slots.
• Exactly 3 interview slots fall between the interviews of Lata and Aditi.
• Gita and Kiran attend in consecutive interview slots.

stimuli.title: Kiran, Isha, Aditi, Jaya, Ovi, Esha, Meera, Uma occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.

questions.stem:
Statements: U < Q > T < V > P.
Conclusions: I. Q ≤ U   II. T ≤ P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. T < X   II. X ≤ U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem: A is the brother of F. F is the mother of E. B is the father of A and F. How is A related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of E’s mother F. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the mother of H. G is the son of H. C is the father of H. How is G related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. C is a parent of H, and G is H’s son. Hence G is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of G. G is the father of E. B is the son of E. A is the sister of G. How is G related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of E, and E is B’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit banking rural = ka su ze
credit access secure = ni ze pa
banking access growth = su to pa
rural secure growth = ka to ni
credit banking growth = to su ze
What is the code for “secure”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ni. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = ze, banking = su, rural = ka, access = pa, secure = ni, growth = to.

questions.stem:
Statements: No lockers is a files. Some files are accounts. All accounts are deposits.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are deposits.
II. Some deposits are files.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are files. Some files are accounts. All accounts are deposits.
Conclusions:
I. All lockers are deposits.
II. No files is a deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some lockers are files. All files are accounts. No accounts is a deposits.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are accounts.
II. Some files are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few lockers are files. All files are accounts. No accounts is a deposits.
Conclusions:
I. Some lockers are not files.
II. No files is a deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 51 km north, turns left and walks 44 km, then turns left and walks 18 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 55. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 33 km along the initial direction and 44 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(33² + 44²) = 55 km.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 22 days and B in 33 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 17. Use 66 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 66 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1800. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 25% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2812.5. Selling price = 1800 × 125/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2812.5.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 6 years, their combined age will be 72 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 12 = 72; x = 15, so father = 45.

questions.stem: The average of 24 numbers is 41. One number, 53, is replaced and the average rises by 8. What is the new number?
